text:
devon: Heads up — customer AcmePay opened a support ticket: intermittent 502/504s from /v1/generate since ~22:10 UTC, SLO alert triggered p99 latency spike. link: https://support.redwood/acme/1234 :eyes:
ash: looping in SRE — customer says retries make it worse, they see long DNS/handshake times then 504s
maya: I can see an SLO burn in grafana (region: eu-west-1). p50 fine, p99 jumps at 22:09 and then again 22:18 — looks bursty not sustained.
ben: can you share a sample trace id? I'll check span coverage.
devon: trace id from their payload: trace-0a1b2c3d — permalinks added to the ticket. Also repro curl below they sent:
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"input":"test"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n"
# they ran in a loop and saw 502, 504, 200 interleaved
```
tracing-bot: Added tracing dump for trace-0a1b2c3d. Noted trace gap between edge-proxy and model-proxy (no spans for 22:09:12 -> 22:09:15).
sre-oncall: I pulled logs for that trace window. ingress logs show connection reset to upstream at 22:09:13 repeatedly. Upstream (model-proxy) responded with 524/empty body at the same time.
ben: query I ran (jaeger/logs):
```
service:edge-proxy | trace_id:trace-0a1b2c3d | level:WARN | message:/v1/generate upstream reset | count>20
service:model-proxy | trace_id:trace-0a1b2c3d | level:ERROR | message:kv-cache miss + async prefetch timeout 120ms
```
maya: interesting — prefetch TTL/queue depth might be the culprit. We recently bumped prefetch concurrency in eu-west routing policy last week. Could be a regress.
ash: customer also noted auth errors around same time for some requests (401s), but mostly 5xx. Could be token rotation inconsistencies on client side + retries hitting throttled path.
devon: support attached token header examples. They are using short-lived tokens from our portal with 60s lifetime.
sre-oncall: for immediate mitigation: can we temporarily route AcmePay traffic to the stable routing policy (no prefetch bump)? Also enable model fallback to smaller quant variant for that customer.
ben: I can open a route override for their org id to stable-policy now. doing: `POST /api/v1/internal/routes/override {org:acmepay, policy:stable-eu}`
ops-bot: Route override queued, rollout id ro-20260316-42 — will apply in ~30s. :thumbsup:
trace-bot: Observability note: adding a synthetic probe for /v1/generate in eu-west to run every 15s.
maya: follow-up actions: 1) check prefetch concurrency change in last deploy (PR #1984), 2) run load-replay with their request pattern, 3) check KV cache hot keys and eviction churn.
ash: I'll keep CS updated and ask customer to hold off aggressive retries while we triage.
devon: thanks. If SLO burn continues for >15m we escalate and open a pager. For now tracking in ticket and will update. :white_check_mark:
ben: quick note — I saw a related minor spike in billing-auth service around 22:08 that could explain transient 401s. I'll correlate logs.
sre-oncall: summary: temporary route override applied, tracing gap confirmed ingress->model-proxy, likely prefetch/concurrency regress. Next: revert prefetch config on canary, run replay, and keep an eye on p99 for 30m.
nash: created a brief postmortem stub in ops repo: https://ops.redwood/incident/IN-2026-0316-acme-edge-timeouts
